key_concepts: Environmental problems include litter, polluted streams, and air pollution.
Air pollution can harm plants, animals, and people.
Science can be used to identify and solve environmental problems.
Proposed solutions should be tested on a small scale before wider implementation.
Community gardens can improve air quality and add green spaces in cities.
Plastic pollution harms animals and clogs rivers and oceans.
Biodegradable materials break down naturally over time and leave no harmful residue.
Non-biodegradable plastics persist in the environment and cause harm.
Replacing single-use plastics with biodegradable alternatives reduces plastic pollution.
Clean-up drives, community education, and petitions help reduce environmental problems.
Scientific information can be gathered through observation, interviews, and research.
